title: Chairing the Tulane Club banquet committee
summary: She loved cooking and was kept as chairman of the banquet committee.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I know you told me you cooked your own fish fries. You're your own fish fries.

Well, when I had the Tulane. Where is that book? I had Tulane Club. I went to California. I was appointed chairman of the club for a banquet. It's right in there. It is. I put it back on top. They just raise up your baby basket. And I said, well, I'm going to California. I ain't going to tell them I'm going. I said, they'll appoint somebody else. I won't be at the meeting. I went to California. I stayed a month. When I came back, the president said, Sister Phillips, you're still chairman of the committee. I said, yeah, I ain't. He said, yeah, you're still chairman of the committee. I said, well, I thought you'd appoint somebody else. He said, no, I want you to be. So I was chairman of that committee and we had 500 people in that club. And I took care of all of that. I had appointed my own committee to work with me. And everybody said I was the best serving they had had. They had had many committees, but I always didn't work on none. I just stayed back, you know, in the background. Cookin' I loved to do it. I always did.
